summary: Defines an XML schema for a video fast update request, used in SIP systems to ask a sender for a fresh full video picture. It documents a method deployed by several vendors before this RFC. New implementations are discouraged from using it and should use the Full Intra Request in RTCP. It is informational.

eli5.summary: If a video call gets garbled, you ask the other side to send a whole new picture. This old method for asking is written down, but newer ways are better.

subtitle: An XML format to request video frames in SIP-based video calls.

tldr.problem: In video calls over SIP, if the video gets corrupted or garbled, the receiver needs to ask the sender for a fresh full video frame, but there was no standard way to request this.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC defines a simple XML schema for a video control command that is sent inside SIP INFO messages. The schema includes a picture fast update command and error reporting.
tldr.outcome: Multiple vendors deployed this method successfully for several years, but RFC 5104 introduced a better method using RTCP feedback that avoids routing through SIP proxies and adds other control functions.

facts.label: Status
facts.value: Legacy; superseded by RTCP-based Full Intra Request

today: This RFC documents a method that was deployed in commercial products but is now superseded by RFC 5104's Full Intra Request mechanism, which uses RTCP instead of SIP. The RTCP approach is more efficient because it avoids routing through SIP proxies and includes additional control functions. RFC 5168 is kept for backward compatibility with legacy systems. New implementations should use RFC 5104.

sections.title: The Problem and the Solution
sections.content:
Video calls using SIP (Session Initiation Protocol) transmit video over RTP (Real-time Transport Protocol). Normally this works well, but if packets get lost or corrupted, the video can become garbled until the next complete frame arrives.

To recover faster, the receiver can ask the sender to send a complete new frame immediately instead of waiting. This command is called a picture fast update or intra frame request.

This RFC documents an XML-based method that was deployed by Microsoft, Polycom, Radvision and others in shipping products starting around 2005. The XML is sent inside SIP INFO messages. However, the RFC explicitly states that new implementations should not use this method. Instead, they should use the Full Intra Request mechanism defined in RFC 5104, which operates through RTCP (Real-time Control Protocol) instead of SIP.
sections.eli5: When video gets scrambled, one side can tell the other to send a fresh picture. This document shows an old way to do it, but newer products use a better system.

sections.title: Video Frames and the Need for Recovery
sections.content:
Video codecs produce frames that come in two types: Intra frames (or I-frames) contain a complete picture and are larger. Inter frames (or P- and B-frames) contain only the changes from the previous frame and are much smaller.

Encoders send mostly inter frames to save bandwidth. However, if the network loses packets for an inter frame, the decoder cannot reconstruct the missing information and the video becomes corrupted.

The receiver can request an intra frame to recover: the next intra frame will restart with complete picture information. However, intra frames are large and sending them uses significant bandwidth. The system must check available capacity before sending one in response to a fast update request.

RFC 4585 introduced RTCP feedback mechanisms for more responsive loss reporting. RFC 5104 extended this to include the Full Intra Request command, which is the recommended approach going forward.
sections.eli5: Video uses two kinds of frames: complete pictures (big) and updates (tiny). When corruption happens, you ask for a complete picture, but only if the network has room for it.

sections.title: The XML Schema
sections.content:
The schema is simple. The root element is <media_control>, which contains zero or more <vc_primitive> elements (video control primitives) and zero or more <general_error> elements.

Each <vc_primitive> contains a <to_encoder> element with the command. Currently, only one command is defined: <picture_fast_update/>. The primitive may also include a <stream_id> to target a specific stream in a multi-stream session.

For errors, the <general_error> element holds free-text error descriptions for problems like XML parsing errors, unsupported media control features, or failure to execute the requested action. Error responses must not themselves generate error responses.
sections.eli5: The XML message is short: it says "hey encoder, send me a fresh picture" or "I had a problem parsing your last message."

sections.title: How It Works in SIP
sections.content:
The SIP INFO method (defined in RFC 2976) is used to carry this media control schema. The sender sets the Content-Type to application/media_control+xml.

A typical use case: Alice's video call is experiencing packet loss and her video decoding is corrupted. Alice's phone sends a SIP INFO message containing the picture fast update command to Bob's phone. Bob's encoder receives the request and sends a new intra frame.

One limitation: if SIP INFO is used for transport, error responses must be sent in separate INFO messages. The SIP protocol only allows 200 OK as a final response to INFO requests, so error replies flow as new SIP transactions.

If errors occur during parsing or execution, the receiver sends a general error message back. However, if the receiver gets an error in response to a fast update request, it should not send further fast update requests in the current dialog, since the remote end may not support the feature.
sections.eli5: The message travels through SIP, which passes it to both SIP phones. The receiving phone reads it and tells its camera to send a fresh frame.
